facts.statement: Hesperosuchus is an extinct genus of crocodylomorph reptiles containing only one species, Hesperosuchus agilis.
facts.quote: Hesperosuchus is an extinct genus of crocodylomorph reptile that contains a single species, Hesperosuchus agilis.

facts.statement: Hesperosuchus belongs to the superorder Crocodylomorpha.
facts.quote: superordo: Crocodylomorpha

facts.statement: Hesperosuchus is classified within the unranked family Sphenosuchia.
facts.quote: unranked_familia: Sphenosuchia

facts.statement: Hesperosuchus was discovered in Northern Arizona by Llewellyn I. Price, William B. Hayden, and Barnum Brown between 1929 and 1930.
facts.quote: Hesperosuchus was discovered in upper Triassic rocks of Northern Arizona by Llewellyn I. Price, William B. Hayden, and Barnum Brown in the fall of 1929 and the summer of 1930.

facts.statement: Remains of Hesperosuchus have been found in Late Triassic (Carnian) rock layers in Arizona and New Mexico.
facts.quote: Remains of this pseudosuchian have been found in Late Triassic (Carnian) strata from Arizona and New Mexico.

facts.statement: Hesperosuchus had large, strong hind limbs and smaller, more slender forelimbs.
facts.quote: The hind limbs of Hesperosuchus are large and strong, while the forelimbs were smaller and more slender.

facts.statement: Hesperosuchus possessed five fingers on its forelimbs and presumably five on its hindlimbs.
facts.quote: Hesperosuchus had five fingers on its forelimbs, and presumably the same on its hindlimbs.

facts.statement: Hesperosuchus had long, slender limbs and a light body weight that allowed it to move very quickly.
facts.quote: This, coupled with its long, gracile limbs and overall light weight, made Hesperosuchus very quick and able to move rapidly.

facts.statement: The skull of Hesperosuchus was tall and narrow, resembling theropod dinosaurs more than modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: It was tall and narrow, more closely resembling the skulls of theropod dinosaurs than modern crocodilians.

facts.statement: Hesperosuchus had lanceolate-shaped teeth that were serrated on both edges and varied in size along the jaw.
facts.quote: The teeth were of lanceolate shape, and serrated on both the front and back edges; these varied in size throughout the mouth.

facts.statement: The front of Hesperosuchus's lower jaw was vertically expanded, featuring four taller teeth, with the fourth tooth being notably enlarged.
facts.quote: The front of the lower jaw (dentary) was vertically expanded, with the first four teeth being higher than the rest behind them, and the fourth tooth was enlarged

facts.statement: Hesperosuchus had two paired rows of roughly square osteoderms along its back, with each bone overlapping the one behind it.
facts.quote: Like most pseudosuchians and basal crurotarsans, Hesperosuchus had two paired rows of osteoderms along its back, with each roughly square osteoderm overlapping the one behind it.

facts.statement: The osteoderms of Hesperosuchus possessed a straight, raised keel on their upper surface.
facts.quote: These possessed a straight, raised keel on its dorsal surface.

facts.statement: Hesperosuchus was a terrestrial animal for which speed and the ability to run fast were key survival traits.
facts.quote: Hesperosuchus was a terrestrial animal, where its speed and ability to run fast is the most advantageous as a fitness trait.

facts.statement: During the Triassic, the landscape of Northern Arizona where Hesperosuchus lived was surrounded by lakes and streams.
facts.quote: Northern Arizona's landscape during the Triassic period was surrounded by numerous bodies of water like lakes and streams.

facts.statement: Hesperosuchus lived at the same time as Coelophysis, a primitive predatory theropod dinosaur.
facts.quote: Hesperosuchus was a contemporary of Coelophysis, a primitive predatory theropod dinosaur.

facts.statement: Bones previously thought to be juvenile Coelophysis found in adult stomachs were later identified as belonging to Hesperosuchus or a similar animal.
facts.quote: However, in some of these cases, it was later found that the "juvenile Coelophysis" bones were actually those of a Hesperosuchus (or something very similar) instead.

facts.statement: It is debated whether later specimens found in the same formation belong to H. agilis, as the time gap between them is at least 20 million years and species differentiation is difficult without complete skeletons.
facts.quote: The referral of these specimens to H. agilis has been doubted, considering the temporal disparity between them (of at least 20 million years), and the consistent morphology of basal crocodylomorphs throughout time, making differentiation between species difficult without complete skeletons.

facts.statement: The dentition and jaw structure of Hesperosuchus suggest it may have had lips to protect its teeth.
facts.quote: Ziphodont dentition and theropod-like pattern of linearly arranged jaw foramina of Hesperosuchus suggest a possible existence of lips that protected its teeth from the outside.

facts.statement: Hesperosuchus is an extinct genus of sphenosuchian crocodyliform containing the single species Hesperosuchus agilis.
facts.quote: Hesperosuchus es un género extinguido de cocodrilomorfo esfenosuquio que contiene una única especie, Hesperosuchus agilis.

facts.statement: Fossilized stomach contents show that Hesperosuchus was part of the diet of the dinosaur Coelophysis.
facts.quote: Este animal formaba parte de la dieta del dinosaurio Coelophysis, como ha mostrado el contenido fosilizado de estos animales.

facts.statement: Remains of Hesperosuchus have been found in Arizona and New Mexico.
facts.quote: Los restos de Hesperosuchus se han encontrado en Arizona y Nuevo México.

facts.statement: Hesperosuchus lived from the Norian to the Rhaetian stages, between 227.3 and 201.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Rhaetian (227.3 to 201.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: Hesperosuchus belongs to the parent group Crocodylomorpha.
facts.quote: Parent group: Crocodylomorpha

facts.statement: Hesperosuchus is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Hesperosuchus is Hesperosuchus agilis.
facts.quote: Type species: Hesperosuchus agilis

facts.statement: The genus Hesperosuchus was named by Colbert in 1952.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Hesperosuchus (genus), Colbert 1952

facts.statement: In at least one case, bones previously thought to be juvenile Coelophysis were proven to belong to Hesperosuchus or a very similar species.
facts.quote: En al menos uno de estos casos, se ha demostrado que los huesos de los supuestos "Coelophysis" jóvenes eran en realidad los de Hesperosuchus (o de una especie muy similar).

rejected.statement: Although once thought to be an ancestor of carnosaurian dinosaurs due to skull and neck similarities, Hesperosuchus is now known to be more closely related to crocodilians.
rejected.quote: Because of similarities in skull and neck anatomy and the presence of hollow bones, Hesperosuchus was formerly thought to be an ancestor of later carnosaurian dinosaurs, but based on more recent findings and research it is now known to be more closely related to crocodilians rather than dinosaurs.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'is now known to be more closely related'

rejected.statement: Hesperosuchus was a relatively small, quadrupedal animal with erect limbs and a digitigrade stance on its hands and feet.
rejected.quote: Hesperosuchus was relatively small, quadrupedal animal with erect limbs, and a digitigrade stance on both hands and feet
